newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban accuse foes of executing prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban accuse foes of executing prisoners.

text.p: Afghan Islamic Taleban militia accused northern opposition forces on Sunday of executing 10 prisoners and wounding one, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted a Taleban spokesman, Wakil Ahmed, as saying 10 Taleban prisoners had been shot dead and one wounded on July 3 in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, where hundreds of Taleban fighters were taken prisoners in late May by forces of opposition leader General Abdul Malik.
He said Mazar-i-Sharif authorities took 11 Taleban prisoners from the central jail to a suburb and shot them, killing all but one on the spot.
The wounded survivor, Mullah Shahzada, escaped and narrated the episode to the Taleban, he said.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report nor a comment from the northern opposition alliance.

The Taleban government's Foreign Ministry has complained to the International Committee of the Red Cross about the incident and urged it to use its influence to ensure that such a thing did not happen again, Ahmed said.

The Taleban forces had briefly captured Mazar-i-Sharif in late May with the help of Malik, who later turned against the purist Islamic militia and ousted it from the city in alliance with the Shi'ite Moslem Hezb-i-Wahdat faction.
